note: Sharp and flat keys mixed (keys:4): both ways round the circle from C, then from a key to its signature on the piano, then from a signature back to its key. The old Key choice on the piano is moves (any key): the piano follows the player's key, named only as {{=key}}, while both circles are pinned to C, where the counting starts. No game shows a signature and asks for its key, so the signatures to name are said in the text and checked on the circle.

exercise.title: Sharp keys and flat keys, both ways
exercise.why: Clockwise from C each key adds a sharp and anticlockwise each adds a flat, so a key's place on the circle gives its signature, and a signature gives the place.

cells.text:
The circle of fifths below starts on C, the key with no sharps and no flats. Say how many sharps G has, then press G to check in the middle of the circle. Do the same for D, A and E, clockwise from C.
Then go anticlockwise from C, through F, B♭, E♭ and A♭, and say the flats the same way.
If you lose count, press C and count the places out from it again.

cells.heading: From the key to its signature

cells.text:
The piano below shows {{=key}} major. Say how many sharps or flats the key has, and which ones, then tap up the scale from {{1}} and count the black keys to check.
Practice until the answer comes before you count.
{{?key}}In another key the black keys are new, and their count is still the number of places from C on the circle.

cells.heading: From the signature to the key

cells.text:
Now go the other way, on the circle below. Say the key with three sharps, then press it and read the middle of the circle to check. Do the same for two flats, four sharps, one flat, two sharps and four flats.
Practice until you can name a key from its signature without counting round the circle.
